title: Anthromes parameters

year.title: Year
year.description: The 75 HYDE 3.2 time steps: every thousand years, then every century, then every decade, then every year. The timeline ends at 2017 because no HYDE release we could obtain carries input grids for 2018 to 2025.

colour_by.title: Color by
colour_by.description: What the color means: the anthrome class; the used fraction of each cell; population density; or where your classification disagrees with the published method run at native resolution before aggregating. At the default thresholds that last difference is purely what aggregating a threshold rule does.

used_threshold.title: Used-land threshold
used_threshold.description: The share of a cell's land that must be cropped, grazed or built before the cell counts as used at all. The published value is 20%. This is the threshold that decides the crossover year, the first time step at which used land exceeds wild, and moving it shifts that year by millennia.

crops_threshold.title: Cropland threshold
crops_threshold.description: How much of a cell must be cropland before the cell is a cropland anthrome. Published value 20%.

grazing_threshold.title: Grazing threshold
grazing_threshold.description: How much of a cell must be pasture or rangeland before the cell is a grazing anthrome. Published value 20%. The reference code keeps this separate from the crops threshold, so the sandbox does too.

rice_threshold.title: Rice threshold
rice_threshold.description: In cells above the dense-settlement population density, the share of irrigated rice that makes the cell a rice village. Published value 20%.

irrigation_threshold.title: Irrigation threshold
irrigation_threshold.description: The irrigated share that distinguishes irrigated villages and residential irrigated croplands from their unirrigated counterparts. Published value 20%.

urban_fraction_threshold.title: Urban area threshold
urban_fraction_threshold.description: The built-up share that makes a cell urban outright, whatever its population. Published value 20%.

urban_density.title: Urban density
urban_density.description: People per square kilometer of land above which a cell is urban regardless of built-up area. Published value 2,500.

dense_settlement_density.title: Dense settlement density
dense_settlement_density.description: The lower edge of the dense-settlement and village band. Below it a cell can't be a village however much rice it grows. Published value 100 per square kilometer.

residential_density.title: Residential density
residential_density.description: The lower edge of the residential band: residential croplands, rangelands and woodlands. Published value 10 per square kilometer.

populated_density.title: Populated density
populated_density.description: The line between populated and remote. Below it a cropland is remote cropland however it's farmed. Published value 1 per square kilometer.

tree_biomes.title: Forested biomes
tree_biomes.description: How many of the fifteen potential-vegetation classes count as potentially forested. The classes are ordered from tropical evergreen forest down to polar ice, and the published cascade draws the line after class 8. Moving it redraws the woodland-dryland boundary of every seminatural and wild cell.

$comment: Slider granularity is x-step, never multipleOf - see bathtub's schema for why. The year is an enum of 75 HYDE time steps drawn as a slider over the stop index (x-control: slider); the value stays the enum member so validation is unchanged. Property order is the panel's reading order: the clock and the view, then the six land-use thresholds with the used-land one first, then the four density cutoffs, then the one vegetation control.
